research_mode: official Home Office and ONS primary statistical publications only; every claim carries a fail-closed limitation; no parcel score, exact incident location, candidate value or business result

sources.name: Special constables and volunteer caution
verified_claims: There were 5,196 special constables and 6,035 police support volunteers by headcount; the bulletin cautions that these figures can fluctuate when forces clean inactive records.
limitations: Headcount fluctuations and absence of contracted hours make these figures unsuitable for parcel-level capacity inference.

sources.name: Officer length of service
verified_claims: At 31 March 2026, 43,525 officers had less than five years of service, representing 29.4% of officers; 53.0% had less than ten years of service.
limitations: Length-of-service data are labelled Official Statistics rather than Accredited Official Statistics because of data-quality issues.

sources.name: Crime QMI revision and designation
verified_claims: The Crime in England and Wales Quality and Methodology Information report was revised on 23 July 2026 and covers accredited official statistics and official statistics.
limitations: Statistical designation varies between component series and must not be applied uniformly.

sources.name: Crime data collection
verified_claims: The CSEW is a face-to-face survey of around 31,000 people aged 16 or over, while police recorded crime is an administrative count of notifiable crimes reported to and recorded by police.
limitations: Survey estimates and administrative records have different populations, error structures and uses.

sources.name: Two main crime sources
verified_claims: The quarterly Crime in England and Wales bulletin uses the CSEW and police recorded crime as its two main data sources.
limitations: The two sources should be interpreted together but not treated as interchangeable measures.

sources.name: CSEW coverage exclusions
verified_claims: The CSEW does not cover crimes against businesses, people not resident in households, homicide or offences often described as victimless such as drug possession.
limitations: Excluded crime types and populations cannot be inferred from CSEW household estimates.

sources.name: CSEW response rate
verified_claims: The provisional CSEW response rate for the year ending March 2026 was 48%; the ONS quality review found little impact on the reliability of crime estimates.
limitations: The lower response rate remains a quality consideration and does not remove sampling uncertainty.

sources.name: Police recorded crime supply
verified_claims: Police recorded crime figures are supplied through the Home Office by the 43 territorial forces and British Transport Police.
limitations: Differences in recording practice and police activity can affect comparability between forces and periods.

sources.name: Notifiable offence boundary
verified_claims: Police recorded crime coverage follows the Notifiable Offence List and excludes non-notifiable matters such as anti-social behaviour and parking offences.
limitations: Excluded incidents must not be silently added to or inferred from notifiable crime totals.

sources.name: Incomplete crime counts
verified_claims: Neither the CSEW nor police recorded crime provides a complete count of crime; both have exclusions and supplementary sources are used for a fuller picture.
limitations: A combined national picture still does not create exact incident or parcel attribution.
